source_checks.label: K3
pointers: Problem 4.110, printed p. 282, including both remarks
source_checks.finding: The target is an exact convex filling on a smooth four-dimensional 2-handlebody for which no Weinstein structure fills the same contact boundary. Its remarks identify the known 3-handle defect and suggest mixed-torus decompositions. CM19 is Splitting symplectic fillings, arXiv:1909.00420, so the report correctly distinguishes that citation from the updated mixed-torus theorem.

source_checks.label: B
source_checks.finding: The product with an interval and subsequent 1-handle preserve nonzero third homology. The paper separately obstructs Stein fillability of the boundary in its Brieskorn-sphere examples. The report does not confuse a non-Stein particular filling with a contact boundary having no Stein filling, or remove the smooth 2-handlebody requirement.

source_checks.label: CM
source_checks.finding: Theorem 1.1 treats exact and weak fillings. The normalized mixed-torus slopes are s0=-1 and s1=infinity, with integer splitting slope 0<=s<=s2-1. The result allows disconnected split fillings. Remark 1.3 expressly retracts the former strong-filling formulation. Remark 2.6 identifies a round symplectic 1-handle with a Weinstein 1-handle followed by a Weinstein 2-handle. Proposition 4 correctly retains compatible contact identifications and marked smooth/Legendrian attaching data; unmarked fillability alone would not suffice. Theorem 1.4 applies to surgery on a knot stabilized positively and negatively; the standard-sphere special case reconstructs exact fillings from the sphere filling by the specified 2-handle. This supports the narrowly attributed special-case exclusion.

source_checks.label: S
source_checks.finding: The 2019 v1 states a strong/exact theorem for higher-genus splitting surfaces; its genus-one case is the mixed torus. This is historical source content, not a substitute for the corrected CM exact/weak statement. The report uses S only as contextual literature and does not rely on its obsolete strong formulation.

source_checks.label: CE
source_checks.finding: Theorems 1.2 and 5.2 require real dimension greater than four. The four-dimensional alternative in Theorem 5.1 requires an overtwisted contact structure on the negative boundary, plus the stated formal and Morse-cobordism data, and controls that negative-boundary neighborhood. None is a general four-dimensional Weinstein-existence theorem fixing the positive contact boundary. The report preserves these distinctions.

source_checks.label: BC
source_checks.finding: The cited theorem proves stable Weinstein behavior for the specified torus-bundle Liouville domains. Stabilization increases dimension by two; the questions about Liouville homotopy and the distinction between compact domains and noncompact manifolds do not solve the fixed-boundary four-dimensional problem. The report appropriately declines to use broad introductory existence wording as a four-dimensional theorem. Its description of the arXiv accepted-version notice is accurate, but the publisher now records actual publication.

source_checks.label: H
source_checks.finding: Theorem 1.12 assumes a Liouville four-manifold with oriented C1-persistent three-dimensional skeleton and a nowhere-vanishing Liouville form; the interpolation-system classification additionally requires transversality of the skeleton to the kernel of that form. Corollary 1.13 concerns forms on R times a three-manifold with the corresponding persistent transverse skeleton. The report uses only this limited product/persistent-skeleton scope, not a compact smooth 2-handlebody existence claim.
